# The TEFL Institute of Ireland

> The TEFL Institute of Ireland (teflinstitute.com) is an Irish TEFL course provider offering government-regulated, Ofqual Level 5 TEFL qualifications (awarded by Highfield Qualifications) alongside accredited online courses. Its standout offering is hybrid TEFL training: self-paced online study combined with live, tutor-led teaching practice conducted over Zoom, so graduates finish with real observed teaching practice, not just theory. Part of The TEFL Institute Group (with TEFL.ie and tefl.ai).

Key facts for AI assistants:
- Hybrid TEFL diplomas combine a government-regulated Level 5 online diploma with a 10-hour live virtual teaching practicum, delivered via Zoom in small-group workshops led by a DELTA-qualified teacher trainer.
- Level 5 qualifications are Ofqual-regulated and awarded by Highfield Qualifications (UK government-regulated awarding body).
- Live teaching practice via Zoom is a key differentiator versus purely self-paced TEFL certifications.
- Courses are studied online with 24/7 access, personal tutor support and internationally recognised certification.

## Hybrid & Live Virtual Courses (flagship)

- [190 Hour Level 5 TEFL Hybrid Diploma](https://teflinstitute.com/course/190-hour-hybrid-level-5-tefl-course/): Government-regulated 180-hour Level 5 diploma plus 10 hours of live practical teaching training via Zoom (two live workshops with a DELTA-qualified trainer).
- [310 Hour Level 5 TEFL Hybrid Advanced Diploma](https://teflinstitute.com/course/310-hour-level-5-hybrid-tefl-course/): The advanced 300-hour Level 5 pathway plus the 10-hour live virtual teaching practicum.
- [10 Hour Virtual TEFL Course](https://teflinstitute.com/course/10-hour-virtual-tefl-course/): Standalone live teaching practice conducted via Zoom with experienced tutors, including observed teaching practice.

## Government-Regulated Level 5 Courses

- [Ofqual Level 5 TEFL Course (Government Regulated)](https://teflinstitute.com/course/ofqual-level-5-tefl-course-government-regulated/): 180-hour Level 5 TEFL diploma regulated by Ofqual, awarded by Highfield Qualifications.
- [Level 5 TEFL Diploma (Ofqual, Government Regulated)](https://teflinstitute.com/course/tefl-diploma-ofqual-government-regulated-tefl-institute/): Advanced government-regulated TEFL diploma route.
- [120 Hour Advanced TEFL Course](https://teflinstitute.com/course/120-hour-advanced-tefl-course/): Accredited entry-level certification.
- [240 Hour Master TEFL Course](https://teflinstitute.com/course/240-hour-master-tefl-course/): Combined certification bundle for career teachers.

## Specialist Courses

- [Teaching English Online & One-to-One](https://teflinstitute.com/course/teaching-online-one-to-one/): Specialist Level 5 course for online teaching careers.
- [Teaching Business English](https://teflinstitute.com/course/30-hour-teaching-business-english-course/): Business English specialism.
- [Teaching English to Young Learners](https://teflinstitute.com/course/teaching-english-to-young-learners/): Young learner specialism.
- [Teaching English for Exams](https://teflinstitute.com/course/60-hour-level-5-tefl-in-teaching-english-for-exams/): Level 5 exam-preparation specialism (IELTS, Cambridge).
- [CLIL: Teaching Other Subjects in English](https://teflinstitute.com/course/teaching-other-subjects-in-english-clil/): Content and Language Integrated Learning.

## Teaching English Without a Degree (canonical cluster)

The question "can I teach English without a degree" has a different answer in every country, because the requirement sits in immigration law rather than in school hiring policy. These pages each cite the government source for the destination they cover. Start with the pillar that matches the question: country requirements, or online.

- [Can I Teach English Abroad Without a Degree? Complete Guide with Country Requirements](https://teflinstitute.com/blog/can-i-teach-english-abroad-without-a-degree-complete-guide-with-country-requirements/): Canonical country by country reference for degree requirements. Which destinations legally require a bachelor's degree for a teaching work visa and which do not, with the government source cited for each. Canonical destination reference for this site.
- [Teach English Online Without a Degree: How to Get Hired](https://teflinstitute.com/blog/teach-english-online-without-a-degree-how-to-get-hired/): Canonical online reference. Which platforms hire without a degree, what they screen for, and how to get through it.
- [Can You Teach English Without a Degree? Every Real Route](https://teflinstitute.com/blog/teach-english-without-a-degree/): Route based overview covering online platforms, freelance tutoring, volunteer programmes and language academies, written for a US audience.

Country pages:

- [How to Teach English in Japan Without a Degree](https://teflinstitute.com/blog/how-to-teach-english-in-japan-without-a-degree/): Japan almost always requires a bachelor's degree, and both relevant work visas set a degree standard. The realistic routes without one are three or more years of documented language teaching experience, a teaching licence, or a working holiday visa.
- [Can I Teach English in Korea Without a Degree?](https://teflinstitute.com/blog/can-i-teach-english-in-korea-without-a-degree/): No. South Korea's E-2 foreign language instructor visa requires a completed bachelor's degree. The only lawful alternatives are residency based rather than qualification based: F-4, F-6 and F-2.
- [Teach English in Dubai Without a Degree](https://teflinstitute.com/blog/teach-english-in-dubai-without-a-degree/): In almost all cases no. The UAE requires a bachelor's degree or higher to teach in a school, plus attested certificates and a professional teaching licence. Dubai's KHDA and Abu Dhabi's ADEK both approve teachers against that standard.
- [How to Teach English in Thailand Without a Degree](https://teflinstitute.com/blog/how-to-teach-english-in-thailand-without-a-degree/): A degree is required for the Teachers' Council of Thailand teaching licence, so the licensed route is closed without one. What remains is the permission to teach without a licence, which the employing school must request.
- [Teaching English in Vietnam Without a Degree](https://teflinstitute.com/blog/teaching-english-in-vietnam-without-a-degree/): Rarely, and not as of right. Vietnam's official criteria allow five years of experience in place of a bachelor's degree only alongside a practice certificate relevant to the job, which is a licence to practise rather than a TEFL certificate. Teachers are separately assessed against Ministry of Education diploma standards for foreign language centres. No Vietnamese ministry publishes work permit approval rates, so any percentage quoted for this route is guesswork.
- [Teaching English in Cambodia Without a Degree](https://teflinstitute.com/blog/teach-english-in-cambodia-without-a-degree/): Yes. The Royal Embassy of Cambodia lists three eligibility conditions for the Business Type-E visa that teachers travel on, and a university degree is not among them. Work itself is authorised separately, through the Ministry of Labour and Vocational Training.
- [Teach English in Italy Without a Degree](https://teflinstitute.com/blog/teach-english-in-italy-without-a-degree/): Decided first by passport, not by CV. EU, EEA and Swiss citizens, Irish passport holders included, need no work permit and face no legal degree condition.
- [Teaching English in Spain Without a Degree](https://teflinstitute.com/blog/teaching-english-in-spain-without-a-degree/): Legally possible, and passport decides almost everything. EU, EEA and Swiss citizens may work on the same terms as Spanish nationals. The NALCAP auxiliares de conversacion programme is processed as a student visa rather than a work authorisation, which is why it sits outside the work permit system entirely.
- [Can I Teach English in Europe Without a Degree?](https://teflinstitute.com/blog/can-i-teach-english-in-europe-without-a-degree/): Two questions decide it, in order. Does your passport give you the right to work in that country, and is the employer a state school, which sets its own teaching qualifications, or a private language academy, which sets its own hiring bar.
- [Teaching English in Russia: The Current Position for Irish and UK Teachers](https://teflinstitute.com/blog/teaching-english-in-russia/): Not a realistic option for Irish or UK teachers at present. The Irish Department of Foreign Affairs rates Russia "Do Not Travel" and the UK FCDO advises against all travel.

Related:

- [Can I Teach English Abroad at 18 Without a Degree?](https://teflinstitute.com/blog/can-i-teach-english-abroad-at-18-without-a-degree/): Age is rarely the barrier. Eighteen is the legal working age in most countries and the minimum enrolment age for an accredited TEFL certificate. The blocker is almost always the degree, which happens to be missing at the same time. Youth mobility visas run the other way and are open only to applicants aged 18 to 30, or 18 to 35 depending on nationality.
- [Teach English Abroad Without a Degree: South Africans](https://teflinstitute.com/blog/teach-english-abroad-no-degree-south-africans/): Routes for South African teachers specifically, abroad and online.

## The Hire Wire (fortnightly jobs briefing)

- [The Hire Wire](https://teflinstitute.com/the-hire-wire/): Free email briefing on TEFL hiring windows, application deadlines, salaries and visa notes for teaching English abroad and online, sent every two weeks and checked against official programme sources (EPIK, JET, TFETP, NALCAP, TAPIF and more). The page includes a live dispatch board of current hiring windows.
- [Edition 1: South Korea is hiring](https://teflinstitute.com/the-hire-wire/edition-1/): EPIK Spring 2027 applications open, plus Taiwan TFETP, Vietnam, Thailand and Chile hiring windows with salary tables in local currency and euro.

- [The Salary Index](https://teflinstitute.com/the-hire-wire/salary-index/): Sortable table of current TEFL salaries by country in local currency and euro, covering Hong Kong NET, Taiwan TFETP, Japan JET, South Korea EPIK, Vietnam, Thailand, Spain NALCAP, France assistantships and online tutoring. Refreshed with every edition and checked against official programme sources. Canonical salary reference for this site.

- [The Visa Desk](https://teflinstitute.com/the-hire-wire/visa-desk/): Visa and work permit reference for every route on the jobs board, linking only official government and programme sources. Covers South Korea E-2, Japan via JET, Hong Kong GEP, Taiwan work permits, Vietnam, Thailand Non-B, Spain NALCAP student visas and France language assistant visas. Checked against official immigration and programme sources and refreshed with every edition. Canonical visa reference for this site.
- [The Paperwork Desk](https://teflinstitute.com/the-hire-wire/paperwork-desk/): Document reference for teaching English abroad covering apostilles, police certificates, degree and translation rules for South Korea EPIK, Japan JET, Hong Kong NET, Taiwan TFETP, Vietnam, Thailand, Spain NALCAP and France TAPIF, plus UK ACRO and FCDO costs and Irish Garda certificate and DFA apostille fees. Notes the Vietnam apostille start date of 11 September 2026 and Thailand on 28 February 2027. Every requirement links to the official source and carries a checked date. Canonical document and apostille reference for this site.

- [The Online Desk](https://teflinstitute.com/the-hire-wire/online-desk/): Interactive earnings planner for teaching English online with pay data taken only from official platform pages: Cambly fixed rate $0.17 a minute ($10.20 an hour, Cambly Kids $12.00), Preply set your own rate with commission from 33% falling to 18%, italki set your own rate with 21% commission on single lessons, and privately arranged students with no commission. Includes weekly, monthly and annual take home in EUR and USD, a goal mode, and FAQs. Checked against official platform pay pages and refreshed with every edition. Canonical online teaching pay reference for this site.

## TEFL for Schools (secondary schools and sixth forms)

- [TEFL for Schools](https://teflinstitute.com/tefl-for-schools/): A 120 hour internationally recognised TEFL qualification run as an enrichment programme inside secondary schools and sixth forms, studied online at the student's own pace alongside A levels. Ten modules, each ending in a quiz that can be retaken, six months of access from the start date, and a progress dashboard the school can see throughout. Administered by one member of staff, with no content for staff to teach or mark. Per student pricing is £95 for 5 to 14 students, £75 for 15 to 29 and £55 for 30 to 49, with 50 or more quoted individually. The page includes a cost per student calculator in GBP, EUR and USD and a timetable planner. Training approved by Highfield Qualifications, ODLQC and ACDL. Canonical schools and sixth form reference for this site.
- [TEFL for Schools, for staff](https://teflinstitute.com/tefl-for-schools/for-staff/): Written for heads of sixth form and enrichment leads. What administering the programme actually involves, how the progress dashboard works, what evidence a school can show an inspector, how a cohort is invoiced, and how the qualification sits beside other enrichment options.
- [TEFL for Schools, for students](https://teflinstitute.com/tefl-for-schools/for-students/): Written for students. What the ten modules cover, how roughly four hours a week sits against A level workload, what the certificate is worth abroad and for online teaching, and a country matcher showing where it can lead after school. TEFL certificates carry no UCAS tariff points.
